Parser for snapshot manifest fields with validation and state-driven decoding.

# Purpose
This file implements the state machine for `fd_ssmanifest_parser`, which reads a serialized snapshot manifest and writes the decoded values into an `fd_snapshot_manifest_t` structure. The parser handles many manifest sections, including blockhash data, ancestors, hard forks, vote accounts, stake delegations, epoch stakes, accounts database metadata, and optional fields such as `hashes_per_tick`, `bank_incremental_snapshot_persistence`, `epoch_account_hash`, and `accounts_lthash`. It also tracks nested array lengths, variant tags, and option fields so it can parse the binary stream in order and place each field into the correct destination.

The main parser flow is split into helper functions that define the size of the current field, the destination pointer for the current field, validation rules, and state transitions after each field is read. [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_consume`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_consume>) copies input bytes into the current destination, checks field validity, advances the state machine, and can also update account-vector metadata through `acc_vec_map_t` and `acc_vec_t`. The file exposes the parser allocation and life-cycle functions [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_align`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_align>), [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_footprint`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_footprint>), [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_new`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_new>), [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_join`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_join>), and [`fd_ssmanifest_parser_init`](<#fd_ssmanifest_parser_init>), so other code can create and use the parser as a reusable component.
